clue.text: Will's supplementary bit of fish — one caught on one line

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
L is a standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone's will has an odd extra provision about a fish hooked on a single line.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'Will’s' is possessive: the definition is a supplementary bit belonging to a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is a legal addition that amends or extends a testament after it was first drawn up.

clue.text: Artist's book is framed by Nick

indicators.note: being framed by something means sitting inside its border

parts.note: a nick is a small cut
B is an abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A painter's volume has been put in a frame by a man called Nick.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', so 'Artist' alone is the definition; Nick looks like a name but is a verb-turned-noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubist is a painter of the early twentieth-century movement led by Picasso and Braque.

clue.text: Was behind but determined

definitions.note: verb phrase; the answer is the past tense of dog

explanation.surface: Someone was trailing in a race yet refused to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow at their heels, and a dogged person shows tenacious resolve.

clue.text: Obsession about no. 1 mug colour

explanation.surface: Someone fusses over the shade of their favourite mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' is slang for face, not a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Complexion is the natural hue and tone of facial skin, and mug is informal for the face.

clue.text: Blur challenged to cover rock

indicators.note: the words cover the solution, which lies hidden beneath them

parts.note: spans the end of Blur and the start of challenged

explanation.surface: The band Blur is dared to do a cover version of a rock song.
explanation.walkthrough: Blur is a British pop band, which makes 'cover' and 'rock' look like music terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To lurch is to sway or pitch suddenly, as a ship does when it rocks in heavy seas.

clue.text: One's unfashionable cul-de-sac

parts.note: one is = I am, contracted to I'M

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being out of style, stuck in a dead-end street.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a dead end, literally a road with no way through or figuratively a deadlock.

clue.text: Tastelessness of trendy colour scheme — odd, 'right off!'

indicators.note: right off means the letter standing for right is taken away

parts.note: rum, British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: An interior designer's fashionable palette is judged strange and in bad taste.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM loses R, leaving UM. Rum meaning peculiar is old-fashioned British English.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is improper or unseemly behaviour, a want of good taste and propriety.

clue.text: All the suits put in a case

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a full deck of playing cards
second meaning: stow belongings in luggage

explanation.surface: Every outfit is folded into a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suits' reads as clothing; it is the four card suits.
explanation.definitionFit: A deck of cards holds every suit, and to stow clothes in luggage before travelling is the verb sense.

clue.text: It takes a brave sort to tuck into mixed dips in the form of earth

indicators.note: mixed means jumbled, so the letters are reordered
to tuck into is to slip inside something

parts.note: the letters of dips rearranged, split to take the inner part
a hero is a courageous person

explanation.surface: Only a bold eater would tackle an assortment of dips shaped like soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck into' looks like eating, but signals insertion; 'earth' is the planet, not soil.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet is not a perfect sphere but slightly flattened, a shape geometers call an oblate spheroid.

clue.text: 'Rock group, Queen, wrecked tune' — well said!

definitions.note: phrase describing speech; the answer is an adjective

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken up and needs putting back in a new order

parts.note: Q is an abbreviation for queen, as on playing cards

explanation.surface: A critic complains that rock bands, Queen included, mangled a melody, and praises their own phrasing.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen is also a rock band, which makes it look like part of the rock group.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloquent speech is fluent and persuasive, so something expressed eloquently is articulated finely.

clue.text: High-ranking woman is worthless, say, on the inside

indicators.note: being on the inside means one part sits within the other

parts.note: bum as an adjective means poor or worthless

explanation.surface: A grand lady is dismissed as worthless, perhaps privately.
explanation.walkthrough: EG goes inside BUM. 'Say' is not a homophone signal here but stands for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: A begum is a Muslim noblewoman or lady of rank in South Asia, a title of high status.

clue.text: Leaves set with fancy chic interior

indicators.note: an interior is what lies inside something else

parts.note: a radio set; the inner part splits it as RAD...IO

indicators.note: fancy implies decorated or elaborated, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone departs from a stylish room furnished in elegant fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb meaning departs; it is the noun, salad leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Radicchio is a bitter red-leaved chicory eaten in salads, so its leaves are what you buy.

clue.text: WP feature that wizards find restricting?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a word-processor tool that flags misspelt words
second meaning, whimsical: a curb placed on magic incantations

explanation.walkthrough: WP is word processing. Read the answer as two words and it becomes a check on spells, which a wizard would resent.
explanation.definitionFit: Word-processing software includes a tool that scans text for errors in orthography, a standard program function.

clue.text: Being in favour dulls the tongue

indicators.note: being in means sitting inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of favour and the start of dulls

explanation.surface: Popularity blunts the sharpness of what someone says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' looks anatomical but means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is a language spoken in Pakistan and India, and tongue is a common synonym for language.

clue.text: Meal spot around one: starting point for a heavenly trip

definitions.text: starting point for a heavenly trip

indicators.note: around means wrapped about another part

parts.note: a, the indefinite article meaning one

explanation.surface: A dining place surrounds someone as they set off on a journey to paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly' means into the sky, toward the heavens, not to paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockets heading into space take off from a launch site, where the voyage skyward begins.

clue.text: Oxen, infected with bacteria, worsening

indicators.note: something infected is corrupted or disordered, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A herd of cattle catches a germ and their condition deteriorates.
explanation.definitionFit: To exacerbate is to make a problem more severe, so the noun names an aggravation of something bad.

clue.text: Aggressive Conservative club in bad movie

indicators.note: bad suggests spoilt or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: in places one part inside the other

parts.note: the letters of movie rearranged, opened up to take the inner part
a bat, a club used in sport

explanation.surface: A combative Tory social club appears in a dreadful film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like the social club of the Conservatives, but it is a piece of sporting kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Combative means eager to fight or argue, the same hostile readiness as aggressive.

clue.text: Describing certain atoms, is oxygen at issue?

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
the matter at issue is the topic

explanation.surface: A chemist wonders whether oxygen is the subject under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotopes are variants of an element with differing neutron counts, so isotopic is the adjective for such atoms.

clue.text: Quickly produce a smash hit

definitions.note: verb phrase; the answer is the two-word phrasal verb
definitions.meaning: first meaning: to churn something out fast

explanation.surface: A songwriter rattles off a chart-topping single.
explanation.walkthrough: In the grid it is one word, but the first sense is the phrasal verb in two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock something out is informal for making it rapidly, and a knockout is a stunning success.

clue.text: Brief lapse by one getting on metro is an omen, not a failing

indicators.note: a failing here means a short word of refusal fails, dropping out of its neighbour

parts.note: an elderly person, one getting on in years
M is the sign for a metro station

explanation.surface: A pensioner riding the underground has a momentary memory slip and reads it as a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT loses NO, leaving T. A senior moment is a jokey name for an older person's forgetfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a passing bout of absent-mindedness, a short memory failure attributed to ageing.

clue.text: Member engaged in bitter claim?

indicators.note: being engaged in something means being involved within it

parts.note: bitter is a type of British beer, an ale
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A member of a group involved in an acrimonious assertion.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter here is the British pub beer, not the adjective for a sour mood.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert something without proof, which is to make a claim.

clue.text: Privileged types making military leader go

parts.note: a go is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: Upper-class folk order a commanding officer to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are people of good social standing just below the nobility, a privileged class.

clue.text: Bill goes in to snack

indicators.note: going in means one part is put inside another

parts.note: taken as written, as the outer part
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill heads in for a bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' reads as a man's name; it is an account, abbreviated in the usual way.
explanation.definitionFit: A taco is a Mexican folded tortilla with a filling, a typical light handheld meal.

clue.text: French port cellar constructed with hole

indicators.note: constructed means built up afresh, so the letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: In a French harbour town, a basement is dug out of a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: La Rochelle is a historic Atlantic harbour city on the west coast of France.

clue.text: Looked for missing top — anything at all

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which goes missing

explanation.surface: Someone searched without their hat and found nothing whatever.
explanation.walkthrough: Ought, also spelt aught, is an old word for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Ought is an archaic variant of aught, meaning anything whatsoever, as in for ought I know.

clue.text: Insult club's top circle

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter

explanation.surface: An affront to the head of a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a flat round shape, so it is a circle in outline.

clue.text: If testing includes an aspect of personality

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside

parts.note: the id, a Freudian part of the psyche

explanation.surface: A conditional: psychological testing may take in a facet of character.
explanation.walkthrough: The short 'If' at the start is the definition; the id is Freud's term for the instinctive part of the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Providing works as a conjunction meaning on condition that, exactly as the word if does.

clue.text: Composer's boundless freedom

indicators.note: without bounds means the word loses its outermost letters at each end

explanation.surface: A musician enjoys unlimited freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: LIBERTY drops its first and last letters. The 's is 'is': Composer is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Ibert was a twentieth-century French writer of music, known for orchestral and chamber works.

clue.text: Skin pierced by lice infestation …

indicators.note: an infestation is a swarming mess, so the letters crawl into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's skin is bitten through by a plague of lice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skin pierced by' reads as one phrase, but pierced is the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuticle is the outer layer of epidermis, especially the hardened rim at the base of a fingernail.

clue.text: … because of that dodgy beer drunk by you once

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
something drunk by a person goes inside them

parts.note: thy is the archaic word for your

explanation.surface: Following the previous clue, suspect ale consumed by an old-fashioned speaker is the reason for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You once' points to an archaic form, here the old possessive. The ellipsis only joins the surface to the clue before.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereby is an adverb meaning by that means or as a result, the same as the phrase defining it.
